trickyParts: `dnsutils` is a virtual package in Debian trixie with no candidate of its own (apt-cache policy says Candidate: (none)); apt resolves it to its single provider, bind9-dnsutils. The apt line, the three Dockerfile comments, the shipped notices sentence and the docs all name bind9-dnsutils now, so the notices sentence's /usr/share/doc/<package>/copyright claim is true and the build does not depend on one provider staying unique.

`nc` is not a file of netcat-openbsd: the package ships /usr/bin/nc.openbsd and the alternatives system installs the `nc` name as root during the build. Every gate asks for `nc`; the Job proved /usr/bin/nc resolves in the built image.

`nc -h` and `dig -v` take no --version: nc -h prints its usage and exits 0 (OpenBSD netcat, Debian patchlevel 1.229-1), dig -v prints its version on stderr. Both are in the build's toolchain smoke step in that form.

psql in Debian is a Perl wrapper around the versioned client; it resolves because perl-base is already in the image. The Job ran `psql --version` in the built image and got psql (PostgreSQL) 17.11, so the wrapper works there — this is the one tool the rejected .deb-extraction route could not deliver.
The image's /bin/sh is dash, whose `type` builtin has no -P, so the on-PATH check runs as `bash -c 'type -P …'` inside the Job rather than from the harness's shell.

The capability row was extended rather than added: a row renders as name, status and detail with no tool list, so packages/contracts/src/legion-api.ts, the daemon API golden fixture and the end-to-end scripts that enumerate rows by name are untouched.

Review round 1 (REQUEST_CHANGES at afb6d68840543a123e32e1496c4e9f54efaa31d4) found four documentation defects, all answered at this head and dispositioned in the pull request comment 6389358614: the pin rule bound only the version, so `bunx biome@0.3.3` obeyed it and still ran the squatter; 'you cannot install a sixth' overstated the bar and contradicted docs/solutions/testing/...LEGION-748.md item 5; the psql reason named local-instance.ts as the entry point of `bun run e2e`, which package.json:16 shows it is not; and the size figure was measured against the deployment's pinned digest rather than this branch's base.

The build's final step now pins nc to /usr/bin/nc beside git, flock, legion and gh: nc is the one new name the alternatives system supplies rather than its own package, so the link is what the name resolves through and a base that changed it would pass every other gate. The gate runs before the image is pushed, so the published sha-afa29128061f tag is its proof.

Test round 1 failed this handoff on one clause: 'every other layer differs by at most 2 KB' was false of the manifests the same sentence cites -- layer 11 differs by -3,164 bytes and layer 8 by +2,740. Re-measured by position across all 24 layers: the Debian layer is 8,285,191 of the 8,286,296 total, the other 23 carry 1,105 bytes net, and 3,164 bytes is the largest single difference. docs/kubernetes.md and this handoff now state those bounds; no other figure in the paragraph changed.

discoveredComplexity: The admission policy of the namespace this role can submit Jobs to requires, in this order of refusal: automountServiceAccountToken: false on the pod template, the build compute class in its nodeSelector, runtimeClassName gvisor, activeDeadlineSeconds on the pod template, and a container requesting at least 4 CPU. Each refusal names what it wants, so a server-side dry run finds the next one; the tester can rebuild the Job from this list in five dry runs or fewer.
